title: NEURODEGENERATION, INFANTILE-ONSET, WITH OPTIC ATROPHY AND STRUCTURAL BRAIN ABNORMALITIES 2

intro.text: This entry describes NDOABA2, a form of infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities. The causal gene and the primary reports are not recalled here with enough confidence to state them.

checks.claim: NDOABA2 is a form of infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper never mentions NDOABA2 or a disorder named infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities. It is an exome sequencing study of a cohort with many different neurologic diseases.

paragraphs.text: Infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities is a severe neurologic disorder. Its cardinal features, as the name states, are neurodegeneration beginning in infancy, optic atrophy, and structural abnormalities on brain imaging.

checks.claim: Infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities is a severe neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We provide genetic and functional evidence establishing BORCS5 as a human disease–associated gene responsible for a severe neurological disorder characterized by a broad spectrum of phenotypes
checks.explanation: The paper calls the BORCS5 disorder a severe neurological disorder but does not use the draft's disease name.

checks.claim: Neurodegeneration beginning in infancy is a cardinal feature of infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas missense variants impair lysosomal activity without disrupting lysosomal distribution, resulting in infantile-onset neurodegeneration.
checks.explanation: The paper links infantile-onset neurodegeneration to the missense (and splice-site) patients. Patients with protein-truncating variants instead had a prenatally lethal developmental phenotype. The disease name is not used.

checks.claim: Optic atrophy is a cardinal feature of infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Optic neuropathy was present in all patients.
checks.explanation: The paper reports optic neuropathy or optic atrophy in the missense and splice-site group but does not describe it as a cardinal feature of a named disorder.

checks.claim: Structural abnormalities on brain imaging are a cardinal feature of infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Neuroimaging revealed cerebral atrophy, white matter loss, hypomyelination, small T2-hypointense thalami, thin brainstem, and optic nerve atrophy in 9 individuals
checks.explanation: The paper reports structural brain imaging abnormalities (atrophy, hypomyelination, corpus callosum abnormalities and polymicrogyria), but not under the draft's disease name.

paragraphs.text: The number 2 in the designation means that at least one other genetic form of this disorder exists (NDOABA1). The specific gene underlying NDOABA2 is not stated here because it could not be recalled with confidence.

checks.claim: Infantile-onset neurodegeneration with optic atrophy and structural brain abnormalities is genetically heterogeneous: at least one other genetic form, NDOABA1, exists besides NDOABA2.
checks.evidence_quote: bi-allelic pathogenic variants in BORCS8 were recently identified in 3 unrelated families with an infantile-onset neurodegenerative disorder (MIM 620987).
checks.explanation: The paper mentions a related BORCS8 infantile-onset neurodegenerative disorder (MIM 620987) that resembles the BORCS5 phenotype. It does not call it NDOABA1 or state that this disorder is genetically heterogeneous.
